newsitem.title: USA: US Rep. Taylor says benefits of D.C. plan unclear.
newsitem.headline: US Rep. Taylor says benefits of D.C. plan unclear.

text.p: Rep. Charles Taylor, R-N.C., chairman of the House Appropriations subcommittee on District of Columbia, said Tuesday it was unclear how President Clinton's plan would help the district in problem areas.
"Our committee wants to reduce crime and improve public education in the District. I'm not certain how the Administration's recommendation helps either," Taylor said in a statement.
The White House announced a $3.9 billion five-year federal aid plan for Washington, D.C.
The White House said it was ending the $3.56 billion federal payment to the city that would have been made over that period.
"It appears the President wants the American taxpayers to absorb billions of dollars in additional spending on the District of Columbia," Taylor said.
The committee will study the plan, he said.
